Q: Split 2-dimensional list into a list of dictionaries with ansible A:

This is exactly the use case of community.general.dict

- name: "Split 2-dimentional list into a list of dictionaries."
  vars:
    parent_list:
      - [value1-1, value1-2]
      - [value2-1, value2-2]
    result: "{{ parent_list | map('zip', ['key1', 'key2'])
                            | map('map', 'reverse')
                            | map('community.general.dict') }}"
  debug:
    var: result

gives the result

    -   key1: value1-1
        key2: value1-2
    -   key1: value2-1
        key2: value2-2

[source code]

Q: sql joins fail to produce nice way to access data from query A:

This is hardly a "best practices" topic.

select * from table1 t1 join table t2.nag_id on t1.nag_id is invalid SQL.

  • select * from table1 t1 is fine.
  • join table looks wrong. Table is a reserved word. A table name is expected here.
  • join table t2.nag_id looks even worse. We join tables not columns.
  • on t1.nag_id would interpret the column as a boolean. As nag_id is probably numeric, some DBMS might raise an error, others might try to apply some conversion.

Q: How to add BFCP support to OpalVoIP for dual-stream SIP conferencing with hardware room systems A:

OpalVoIP does not natively support BFCP, so the typical solution is to integrate a third-party BFCP implementation such as libbfcp and bridge it into OpalVoIP through a C++ wrapper.

The wrapper layer:

  • Translates libbfcp callbacks into OpalVoIP call events

  • Maintains BFCP client/server state machines

  • Activates the content (presentation) stream when a FloorGrant is received or issued

BFCP and the content stream should be pre-negotiated in the initial SDP offer, for example:

m=application 50000 TCP/BFCP *
a=floorctrl:c-s
a=confid:1
a=floorid:1 mstrm:3

m=video 53000 RTP/AVP 99
a=content:slides
a=label:3

Avoid mid-call renegotiation, as many hardware endpoints (Cisco, Polycom, Lifesize) handle BFCP inconsistently when it is introduced after call setup.

Implementation Approach

In our deployment we created a wrapper such as:

bfcpinterface.cxx

Responsibilities of this layer:

  • Wrap libbfcp client/server APIs

  • Convert BFCP callbacks → OpalVoIP media events

  • Manage floor control lifecycle

Call Direction Behavior

Outbound call (gateway initiates)

  • Gateway acts as BFCP client

  • Sends FloorRequest

  • Waits for FloorGrant

  • Enables the content stream

Inbound call (endpoint initiates)

  • Gateway acts as BFCP server

  • Receives FloorRequest

  • Sends FloorGrant

  • Enables the content stream

The role is determined by the SDP attribute:

a=floorctrl

Values:

  • c → client

  • s → server

  • c-s → both

Practical Lessons

From production interoperability testing:

  • Always pre-negotiate BFCP

  • Keep client and server state machines isolated

  • Test with real endpoints (Cisco, Polycom, Lifesize) — each has subtle BFCP quirks.

Additional Reference

More details with architecture diagrams and SDP examples:

https://medium.com/@jo.sagar/the-missing-protocol-how-bfcp-unlocked-dual-monitor-conferencing-for-enterprise-room-systems-36e61b336fbf

This integration was used in a production Telepresence Gateway deployment on AWS, but the BFCP support was never merged into the main OpalVoIP codebase.
